sentences.text: Nanyangosaurus was a small herbivorous dinosaur estimated to be 4 to 5 meters long and 1.5 meters high.
Its femur measured 51.7 cm in length.
The animal possessed relatively long forelimbs with a hand that completely lacked the first digit and first metacarpal, a condition present in the living animal rather than due to preservation.
Unlike its relatives, Nanyangosaurus did not possess a thumb spike, though it had three middle hand digits fused to aid in locomotion along with a large thumb ending in a point.
The toes on the hind limbs formed a hoof-like structure.
Remains of Nanyangosaurus were discovered in 1994 near the village of Houzhuang in Neixiang County, Henan Province, China.
The holotype specimen IVPP V 11821 was excavated from the Xiaguan Formation.

The type species Nanyangosaurus zhugeii was described by Xu Xing and colleagues in 2000, with the genus name coming from the city of Nanyang and the species name honoring the legendary strategist Zhuge Liang.
Nanyangosaurus is classified as a herbivorous ornithopod dinosaur within the Hadrosauromorpha.
It is classified within the family Iguanodontidae.
Nanyangosaurus lived during the Turonian to Campanian stages, approximately 93.9 to 72.2 million years ago.
Although initially considered Albian due to its primitiveness, the type horizon of Nanyangosaurus is now believed to be Turonian-Campanian based on associated plant and invertebrate fossils.
